items.text: When a Pulumi Output is treated as if it were already a plain value (e.g. converted to a string), Pulumi substitutes placeholder text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` in place of the value, which can appear in a log line, a generated file, or a resource property.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ ("Output value errors") exists and covers symptoms of treating an output as a plain value.

Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values.
The real value of a Pulumi Output is not known until the resource providing it has been created or updated.
Outputs are central to how Pulumi builds its dependency graph and runs `pulumi preview`.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/ exists with an anchor #outputs.
The pages /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/ (Accessing single outputs with apply) and /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/ (Working with multiple outputs) exist.
Converting a Pulumi Output to a string directly (concatenating, logging) does not raise an error by default; Pulumi silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.
In the Pulumi TypeScript SDK, stringifying an Output yields literal text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, and no exception is thrown.
The TypeScript SDK's toString placeholder message is followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate` instead.

In the Pulumi TypeScript SDK, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an Output (or letting one flow into a JSON body) produces the string `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` rather than the value.
In the Pulumi Python SDK, stringifying an Output (e.g. in an f-string) yields literal text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported` and no exception is raised.
In the Pulumi Python SDK, stringifying an Output also logs a warning.
In the Pulumi Python SDK, passing an Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
The Pulumi Python SDK provides `Output.json_dumps()` for JSON-serializing values that contain Outputs.
In the Pulumi Go SDK, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error rather than a runtime surprise.
In the Pulumi Go SDK, `ApplyT` is the method used to resolve an Output's value inside a callback.
In the Pulumi C# SDK, stringifying an Output (e.g. via string interpolation) yields literal text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` and no exception is thrown.
The C# SDK's ToString placeholder message is followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format` instead.
A Pulumi program that stringifies an Output still runs and `pulumi up` succeeds; the placeholder text only surfaces later in a log line, generated config file, or downstream resource property.
The environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` is supported by the Pulumi TypeScript, Python, and C# SDKs.
With `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` set, stringifying an Output throws an exception at the point of the mistake instead of returning placeholder text.
The Pulumi TypeScript SDK provides `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` as string-composition helpers for Outputs.
The Pulumi Python SDK provides `Output.concat` and `Output.format` as string-composition helpers for Outputs.
The Pulumi Go SDK provides `pulumi.Sprintf` and `pulumi.JSONMarshal` as string/JSON-composition helpers for Outputs.
The Pulumi C# SDK provides `Output.Format` as a string-composition helper for Outputs.

The plain value read out of an Output inside an `apply` callback is only available inside that callback or in another Output derived from it; assigning it to an outer variable and reading it outside the callback does not yield the value.

A Pulumi `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the Output resolves, which is generally after the rest of the program's top-level code has finished running, so an outer variable set inside it is still `undefined` when read at top level.
An `apply` callback runs when the Pulumi engine resolves the dependency graph, not on the program's clock, so adding a delay does not make the value available outside the callback.
Passing an Output directly as a resource input (e.g. `bucket: bucket.bucketName` on `aws.s3.BucketObject`) lets Pulumi resolve the dependency without any `apply`.
Passing an Output itself as the input to whatever needs it is 'usually the better option' compared to doing downstream work inside the same `apply` or chaining a further `apply`.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept Outputs as well as plain values.
A Pulumi resource's logical name cannot be an Output; it must be a known plain value while the program is being evaluated.
The output-values page has a section with anchor #using-an-output-as-a-resource-name-a-map-key-or-a-loop-bound.

In a dynamically typed Pulumi SDK, an `if` statement on an Output evaluates the Output object itself (not its eventual value), so the condition is generally always true regardless of what the Output resolves to.
In a statically typed Pulumi SDK, branching on an Output directly is usually a compile error because an `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.

Values already known at program start — a stack configuration setting read with `pulumi.Config`, an environment variable, or a hardcoded flag — are plain values, not Outputs, and can be branched on normally.

When a branch depends on a resource's Output, the branch must move inside `apply` and both outcomes must be expressed as values (deriving a new Output) rather than as separate blocks of resource-creation code.
A Pulumi resource's logical name is the first argument to its constructor.
Loop bounds and map keys used while authoring a Pulumi program must be known plain values at evaluation time, before any resource exists.
Passing an Output as a resource logical name, loop bound, or map key fails to compile in the Pulumi TypeScript, Go, and C# SDKs, because those positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In the Pulumi Python SDK, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string` at runtime.
In the Pulumi Python SDK, using an Output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.

In the Pulumi Python SDK, using an Output as a dictionary key does not raise; Python hashes and compares the Output object itself, so the lookup silently keys on the object rather than the eventual value.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/ exists with an anchor #stackreferences.
A Pulumi `StackReference` lets one Pulumi program/stack consume another stack's outputs as its inputs.

Pulumi has no supported way to block a program and synchronously read the resolved value of an Output; attempting to `await` or read one synchronously either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.
The CLI command `pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output after a deployment.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/ exists.
The Pulumi Automation API's update result exposes an `outputs` field (e.g. `res.Outputs` in Go) containing the stack outputs after running an update.
